name: Laverton
reason: Rule 1+2, town: the regional board gives Laverton its own page naming The Great Beyond Explorers' Hall of Fame (a museum and visitor centre), the historic police station complex and Giles Breakaway; visitors base here for the Outback Way and Anne Beadell Highway.
objection: Only one counted source (no Wikivoyage page); a remote mining town whose draw for most is the road beyond it, so the proposer may treat it as a gateway at a low rank.

name: Ravensthorpe
reason: Rule 1+2, town: own board page naming the PUBLIC silo art, historic buildings, the Ravensthorpe Range drives and lookouts; the Fitzgerald Coast shire town visitors stop in.
objection: One counted source; its named draws (silo, lollipop, range) are separate candidates, so keeping the town too risks the town-as-wrapper pattern COVERAGE warns against; the wildflower show is an event and does not count.

name: Hopetoun
reason: Rule 1+2, town: own board page; a seaside holiday town on Mary Ann Haven with beaches, the Southern Ocean Road and the eastern gateway to Fitzgerald River NP, where visitors base themselves.
objection: One counted source; much of its pull is Fitzgerald River NP (another region), so it is partly a gateway town.

name: Kellerberrin
reason: Rule 1: own board page naming a folk museum, Kellerberrin Hill Lookout and Kokerbin Rock nearby.
objection: Small Wheatbelt service town on the Great Eastern Highway; its strongest draw (Kokerbin Rock) is 40 km away and would be its own spot; one counted source and no Wikivoyage page; fails the friend test unless passing through.

name: Narrogin
reason: Rule 1+2, town: own board page calling it the base for Dryandra Woodland, with a heritage walk trail, the Old Court House Museum, a mural drive and Foxes Lair reserve; a regional hub visitors stay in.
objection: One counted source; the real draw (Dryandra, Barna Mia) is 22 km away and is its own spot.

name: Wongan Hills
reason: Rule 1: own board page naming the Mount O'Brien lookout, Mount Matilda walk, pioneer museum and spring wildflower reserves.
objection: Small farming town, 671 page views, one counted source; the lookout and walk are 10 km west and the wildflowers seasonal; a traveller from elsewhere goes mainly in wildflower season.

name: Mount Magnet
reason: Rule 1+2, town: own board page; the Murchison hub on the Great Northern Highway with a 37 km tourist trail, Warrmboo Hill views, the Mining and Pastoral Museum and The Granites rock art nearby; a base for the region.
objection: One counted source; a mining town most travellers pass through; the outdoor cinema is summer-only and the races an event.

name: Meekatharra
reason: Rule 1+2, town: own board page; the largest Murchison centre, with a heritage walk, the Rangelands Discovery Trail, museum, State Battery and Peace Gorge 5 km out; travellers on the Great Northern Highway stop and stay here.
objection: One counted source and no Wikivoyage page; Peace Gorge may deserve to be the spot rather than the town.

name: Twilight Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: named on Wikivoyage Esperance (Do) and the regional board (its own 'Twilight Bay' listing, 'rock with a hole'); a swimming beach on the Great Ocean Drive.
objection: No Wikipedia article; one of several beaches on the same coast road, so overlap with the Great Ocean Drive.

name: Blue Haven Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: the board's own listing: a sheltered swimming beach reached by a steep staircase; second-tier beach a real source names.
objection: One counted source; one of a string of beaches on the Great Ocean Drive within a few kilometres.

name: Duke of Orleans Bay
reason: Rule 1: the board's own listing calls it among the most picturesque uncrowded coastal areas; a bay with several beaches, a holiday park and camping.
objection: Wharton Beach, which the board also lists, is the bay's main beach: keeping both risks a near-duplicate (rule 3); keep one (Wharton Beach) unless the owner wants the bay as the broader place.

name: Wharton Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: the board's own listing calls it one of the best beaches in Esperance; a long white beach in Duke of Orleans Bay about an hour east of town.
objection: One counted source; overlaps with Duke of Orleans Bay (kept here as the one spot for the bay).

name: Fourth Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: the board's own listing; a long surf beach popular for water sports on the Esperance coast road.
objection: One counted source; a local surf beach among several adjacent ones (West, Observatory, Twilight).

name: West Beach (Esperance)
reason: Rule 1: named once on the board's Esperance page as a reef-break surf beach.
objection: Only a passing mention for surfers, no listing of its own, one source; adjacent to several stronger beaches on the same drive, so likely only of interest to surfers already there.

name: Observatory Beach
reason: Rule 1: named once on the board's Esperance page as a reef-break surf beach.
objection: Passing mention only; sits beside Observatory Point lookout (kept), so it is close to a near-duplicate of that spot.

name: Munglinup Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: the board names its natural lagoon for snorkelling; a second-tier beach a real source names.
objection: One counted source, a passing mention; remote (about 100 km west of Esperance) with a small campground.

name: Observatory Point
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing and the board's own 'Observatory Point and Lookout' listing; a lookout over the coast and Recherche islands where the French ships sheltered in 1792.
objection: A pull-out on the Great Ocean Drive with a short look (rule 3 roadside caveat), but two guides single it out by name.

name: Esperance Esplanade
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See listing: beachside foreshore parks with views to the port and islands, sculptures (the whale tail) and a children's adventure park.
objection: A town foreshore rather than a distinct draw; one source; could equally be covered in the destination's description; the Tanker Jetty (if a candidate) is the stronger foreshore spot.

name: Esperance Museum
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See listing (rambling collection, 1979 Skylab debris) and the board's own product page; open to the public with paid entry.
objection: Short opening hours (sources conflict: Thu-Sun 1:30-4:30 pm per the Shire); a small local museum whose standout is the Skylab wreckage.

name: Historic Museum Village
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See listing: relocated 19th-century buildings now used as cafes, galleries and shops, the oldest a 1895 church.
objection: Rule 2 risk: what a visitor does is browse shops and cafes; one source; short visit.

name: Esperance Wind Farm
reason: Rule 2/3: Wikivoyage mentions turbines 'seen from afar', 19 km west of town: a roadside view of infrastructure, not a place to spend half an hour, and no listing of its own.
objection: Wikivoyage does mention it in See; if a public viewing area exists it could be a short stop.

name: Esperance Bird and Animal Park
reason: Rule 1+2: the board's own listing: a small wildlife park and cafe 10 minutes from town where visitors pat animals.
objection: One counted source; a small commercial animal park and cafe of local appeal; its coordinates are the Gibson locality's (Wikipedia redirect), not the park's.

name: Esperance Stonehenge
reason: Rule 1-3: the board's own listing; a full-size replica of Stonehenge, a quirky roadside icon travellers stop for and photograph (COVERAGE: quirky landmarks are spots).
objection: One counted source; on private farmland with an entry fee; a short visit.

name: Great Ocean Drive (Esperance)
reason: Rule 1-3: the board's own listing and its suggested itinerary: a 38 km coastal loop from Esperance, the town's signature scenic drive, past Twilight Beach, Observatory Point and the Pink Lake.
objection: A drive, not a single place; its stops (Twilight Beach, Observatory Point, Blue Haven) are candidates of their own, so it partly duplicates them.

name: Lake Monjingup
reason: Rule 1+2: the board's own listing: a lake with a boardwalk, picnic area, bird watching and spring wildflowers.
objection: One counted source; a local nature reserve (Lake Monjingup Reserve) of the 'ordinary reserve near a town' kind COVERAGE leaves out unless guides feature it.

name: Woody Lake Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1+2: the board lists the Woody Lake Nature Reserve Canoe Trail, a waymarked paddle through paperbark channels.
objection: One counted source and it is listed as a product; a local wetland reserve; paddling needs your own canoe or hire.

name: Kepwari Wetland Trail
reason: Rule 1+2: the board's own listing: a 3.6 km interpretive wetland trail five minutes from town.
objection: One counted source; a local wetland walk of the kind locals use; fails the friend test.

name: Archer Drive Lookout
reason: Rule 1: named on the board's Esperance and Ravensthorpe pages: a walking trail and scenic drive to a lookout over farmland and mountains in the Ravensthorpe Range.
objection: Rule 3: likely one of the two lookouts on the Ravensthorpe Range (kept as its own spot), so a part of a larger place; keep one or the other.

name: Dabungool cultural tour
reason: A spot is a place: this is a tour operator (cultural bush-tucker tour), not a place.
objection: It is the region's Aboriginal cultural experience; it belongs in a tip or bio, not as a spot.

name: Cindy Poole Glass Artist studio
reason: Rule 2: a commercial glass studio and gallery (a shop/business), not a spot.
objection: The board does list it as a gallery experience visitors can walk into.

name: Le Grand Beach
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing in Cape Le Grand National Park: a wide white beach with a campsite and the start of the coastal trail to a headland lookout.
objection: Wikivoyage says it lacks the drama of the other bays; one counted source.

name: Thistle Cove
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing: a cove between granite headlands with the 'whistling rock' monolith beside the car park and sculpted boulders.
objection: One counted source; Wikivoyage says it is not good for swimming; a short stop.

name: Rossiter Bay
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See listing and the board's combined 'Mississippi Hill and Rossiter Bay' listing; the 1841 Eyre rescue site at the end of the coastal trail.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says 'the bay is not particularly exciting'; its interest is historical; could fold into Mississippi Hill or the coastal trail.

name: Mississippi Hill
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Do (30-min return walk from Lucky Bay) and the board's 'Mississippi Hill and Rossiter Bay' listing; a summit walk with views over the bays.
objection: A short walk starting at Lucky Bay, so arguably part of the Lucky Bay visit.

name: Mount Le Grand
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Do (3-hr off-track climb, caves on the eastern side) and the board's Cape Le Grand page (rock climbing at Mount Le Grand).
objection: No defined path; a hard climb few visitors do compared with Frenchman Peak.

name: Cape Le Grand Coastal Trail
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Hiking (15 km Le Grand Beach to Rossiter Bay in four sections) and the board ('tackle all or a section of the park's 20 km trail'); a DBCA-promoted day walk.
objection: Its stops (Hellfire Bay, Thistle Cove, Lucky Bay) are spots themselves, so it overlaps them.

name: Sanko Harvest wreck
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Diving listing: the largest diveable wreck on the Australian coast, a marine sanctuary, 12 km south of Hellfire Bay.
objection: Rule 2: reachable only by boat as an experienced diver, so most visitors can do nothing there; reached through dive operators.

name: Woody Island
reason: Rule 1-3: re-looked for a counted source and found DBCA's park page (Woody Island Nature Reserve: three self-guided trails, snorkel trail, the only Recherche island with visitor facilities, cabins and camping); the board also lists Woody Island Eco Tours. The island is the place the ferry goes to.
objection: Seasonal (about August to June) and reached only by the operator's boat; a single operator runs it.

name: Lake Hillier
reason: Rule 1: re-looked: Tourism WA (westernaustralia.com) has an attraction page for it; famous pink lake on Middle Island, 44,580 page views.
objection: Rule 2: there is no public landing; it is seen only from a scenic flight or an occasional cruise, so a visitor cannot stand there; COVERAGE allows 'what a scenic flight flies over' as the spot, which argues for keeping, but nothing can be done on site.

name: Stokes National Park
reason: Rule 1-3: DBCA park page and Wikivoyage article: estuary park with camping, canoeing, fishing, walks and the Moir Homestead ruins.
objection: Low profile (543 views); visited mainly by campers and anglers.

name: Margaret Cove
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Do listing in Stokes National Park: a fairly popular snorkelling and swimming spot.
objection: One counted source, a one-line listing; a small cove of local appeal.

name: Stokes Estuary
reason: Duplicate of Stokes National Park: Stokes Inlet/estuary is the park's main feature and its visitor point.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it separately as a rare landscape.

name: Ravensthorpe Range
reason: Rule 1-3: on the board's Ravensthorpe and Hopetoun pages (own listing): 40 km of hills with two lookouts and drives, a biodiversity hotspot.
objection: A range, not a single point: its lookouts (Archer Drive, Ethel Daw) are the actual stops; the pin must go to one lookout.

name: Mount Short Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: on both board pages: a 40 km four-wheel-drive track to Mount Short, the highest point in the region.
objection: 4WD only; a drive rather than a place (the place is Mount Short); local appeal.

name: Mount Madden Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: on both board pages: a 160 km, five-to-six-hour circuit with views and spring wildflowers at Pallarup Rocks.
objection: A long farmland loop drive, not a place; the place visitors stop at is Pallarup Rocks, which would be the spot if any.

name: Ethel Daw Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: the board's Ravensthorpe page: a drive with 360-degree views of the town, national park, mountains and sea.
objection: Rule 3: likely the access road to a lookout on the Ravensthorpe Range (kept), so part of a larger place; one source.

name: Ravensthorpe PUBLIC Silo
reason: Rule 1-3: the board names the silo artwork (a Banksia's flowering cycle) as an attraction; part of the PUBLIC Silo Trail, a giant roadside artwork travellers stop for.
objection: A short photo stop in Ravensthorpe; if Ravensthorpe town is kept too, avoid a town-and-its-attraction pair.

name: World's Biggest Lollipop, Ravensthorpe
reason: Rule 1-3: the board names it as a photo stop; a quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE: quirky landmarks travellers photograph are spots).
objection: One counted source; stands outside a sweet shop, a five-minute stop; 'world's biggest' is unverified and must not appear in the bio.

name: Hopetoun-Ravensthorpe Railway Heritage Walk Trail
reason: Rule 1-3: on both board pages (with its own listing): a sectioned heritage rail trail between Hopetoun and Ravensthorpe, with a 14 km loop from Hopetoun.
objection: A local heritage trail; long and walked in sections.

name: Beacon Hill Lookout (Hopetoun)
reason: Rule 1: the board's Hopetoun page: a lookout 3 km from town over Hopetoun, the sea and mountains.
objection: One source; a short lookout stop of local appeal (rule 3 roadside caveat).

name: Culham Inlet
reason: Rule 1: the board's own listing: a landlocked estuary west of Hopetoun with fishing and lookouts.
objection: One source; mainly a fishing spot; of local appeal.

name: Jerdacuttup
reason: Rule 1/2: the source names only unnamed 'beaches and camping areas' around a rural community; nothing specific to see, so the town test fails.
objection: The board does name it, and its beaches may be worth a stop for campers.

name: Southern Ocean Road
reason: Rule 1: the board's Hopetoun page: a 72 or 93 km coastal drive east of Hopetoun past lookouts and beaches (Mason Bay, Starvation Bay).
objection: A drive rather than a place, one source; its named beaches would make better spots.

name: Sepucralis Hill Lookout
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-great-southern (it overlooks Hamersley Inlet inside Fitzgerald River National Park, which the boundary brief puts wholly in the Great Southern).
objection: The board lists it on the Hopetoun page; the Great Southern pass must cover it.

name: Mount Barren walk
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-great-southern (East Mount Barren is in Fitzgerald River National Park).
objection: A real 3-hour summit walk the board names; the Great Southern pass must cover it.

name: Hannans North Tourist Mine
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing (open-air museum of early mine buildings and machinery, paid entry) and the board's own listing ('Kalgoorlie's largest open-air museum').
objection: Its coordinates come from the Australian Prospectors & Miners' Hall of Fame redirect; hours and status should be checked in research.

name: Mount Charlotte Reservoir and Lookout
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing (reservoir at the end of the Golden Pipeline, best lookout over the city) and the board's 'Mount Charlotte' listing (easy summit walk, sunset views).
objection: A short lookout stop; partly overlaps the Golden Pipeline story.

name: Paddy Hannan statue
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage See listing: a replica statue of the prospector where visitors traditionally drink from his water-bag fountain.
objection: Rule 3: a statue is close to a minor memorial; one source, a few-minute stop on Hannan Street.

name: Museum of the Goldfields
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage See listing (gold vault, Aboriginal objects, headframe viewing platform) and the board's own listing; a WA Museum site.
objection: Coordinates are wrong: they are the WA Museum's in Perth (Wikipedia redirect); resolve-pin must find the Kalgoorlie building.

name: Boulder Pioneer Cemetery
reason: Rule 3/friend test: a historic pioneer cemetery, one counted source with a one-line listing ('headstones with a story'); a local heritage site, not a draw a traveller goes out of the way for.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it under See, and goldfields cemeteries draw history-minded visitors.

name: Karkula Bushland Park
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Do listing: bushland reserve on the edge of Kalgoorlie with a 4 km loop to an elevated viewing platform.
objection: One source; close to the 'ordinary suburban park' COVERAGE leaves out; Wikivoyage itself mentions the flies and hidden wildlife.

name: Herbert Hoover Mirror
reason: Rule 3: a single object in the foyer of a working hotel (the Palace Hotel), a five-minute look, not a distinct draw; rule 2: the venue is a pub/hotel.
objection: Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder lists it in See with a good story (Hoover's gift to a barmaid); could be mentioned in a Kalgoorlie bio or Hannan Street heritage walk instead.

name: Goldfields Arts Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: one counted source (Golden Outback board, 'hub of the region's arts scene', two galleries and a 700-seat theatre); visitors can see exhibitions for half an hour.
objection: Mainly a performance venue and conference centre; only one counted source and Wikivoyage's Kalgoorlie page does not list it, so the friend test is 'only if you are in Kalgoorlie anyway'.

name: Questa Casa brothel tour
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder Do listing; Kalgoorlie-Boulder Visitor Centre page 'Questa Casa - Australia's oldest brothel'); daily 3 PM tours of the building, a well-known Hay Street curiosity. If kept, the spot is the place, 'Questa Casa', not 'brothel tour'.
objection: A working commercial business (brothel) visited only on a timed adults-only tour; the brief rejects businesses and tours, and the place is otherwise not open to the public.

name: Kalgoorlie Arboretum
reason: Rule 1: DBCA Explore Parks has a page (26 ha arboretum, interpretive walk trails, picnic, birdwatching at the dam); rule 2: half an hour's walk is possible.
objection: Essentially a town park with a dog exercise area, the kind of local reserve COVERAGE leaves out; one counted source; fails the friend test outside a long stay in Kalgoorlie.

name: Burra Rock
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Coolgardie 'Further afield'; DBCA page for Burra Rock Conservation Park): a granite outcrop with a historic woodline catchment wall and dam, relics, picnic and camping.
objection: An unsealed drive south of Coolgardie for a picnic-stop rock; mostly visited by campers and 4WD travellers.

name: Coolgardie Goldfields Exhibition Museum
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it as the place to explore Coolgardie's gold-rush history, and the Shire of Coolgardie's visit page lists it (62 Bayley St, also the visitor centre); rule 2: open daily, a real museum in the Warden's Court building.
objection: Only one counted source in the candidate; shares a building with the Coolgardie Visitor Centre (keep as one spot, the museum, if a visitor-centre candidate also exists).

name: Waghorn Bottle Collection
reason: Duplicate of Coolgardie Goldfields Exhibition Museum: the collection is displayed upstairs in the museum's courtroom (Shire of Coolgardie / museum listings).
objection: The board names it as its own attraction ('Australia's largest display of bottles'); mention it in the museum's bio rather than as a spot.

name: Ben Prior's Park
reason: Two counted sources name it (Wikivoyage Coolgardie See; Golden Outback board 'Goldfields Exhibition Museum and Ben Prior's Park'): a free open-air display of old mining and farm machinery on the main street.
objection: A roadside yard of rusty machinery seen in ten minutes; arguably part of the Coolgardie main-street heritage stop rather than a distinct draw.

name: Coolgardie Cemetery
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Coolgardie See; Golden Outback board): an 1894 gold-rush cemetery with the grave of explorer Ernest Giles, the regional pioneer-cemetery stop guides single out.
objection: A cemetery is a short look; friend test is weak unless already in Coolgardie, and the board also lists a separate Old Pioneer Cemetery (near-duplicate risk).

name: Jack Carin's Camp
reason: Rule 3: a minor site (a ramshackle prospector's hut beside an active mine) named only by Wikivoyage, a few minutes' look; one counted source for a marginal place.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it in See with a story attached, so it is not invisible to visitor sources.

name: Victoria Rock
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Coolgardie 'Further afield' names it (largest hill in the area, easy summit with a view, quiet camping on the Holland Track); a walk up is a half-hour-plus visit.
objection: Only one counted source and 45 km out on a dirt track; mostly a camping spot for Holland Track 4WD travellers.

name: Lion's Lookout
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback board names it (picnic and the view the first prospectors saw over Coolgardie).
objection: One source, a short lookout over a small town; rule 3 short-stop concern and no second source.

name: Cave Hill
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback board names Cave Hill among Coolgardie's outback nature reserves; a granite hill with caves, a camping and 4WD spot in the Great Western Woodlands.
objection: One counted source, 4WD access only, and no detail on what the visitor does there in the source; no DBCA page found (exploreparks 404).

name: Rowles Lagoon
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names the freshwater wetlands at Rowles Lagoon near Coolgardie; a lagoon with birdlife and camping.
objection: One counted source, a single passing mention, and an ephemeral wetland that may be dry; the friend test fails.

name: Red Hill Lookout
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Kambalda See; Golden Outback board): the highest point of Kambalda with a panorama over Lake Lefroy and a 300 m and 1.7 km loop trail - a distinct lookout plus walk, not part of a larger listed spot.
objection: A small-town lookout; its main view is Lake Lefroy, so it and Lake Lefroy should not both be kept as separate views of the same thing.

name: Lake Lefroy
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it (a 40 km salt pan used for land sailing and speed-record attempts, yacht hire by arrangement); 2,583 page views.
objection: Its visitor viewpoint is Red Hill Lookout (kept), so as a view it is a near-duplicate; land sailing is an activity by prior arrangement, not a place a visitor can just turn up to.

name: Kambalda Pioneer Cemetery
reason: Rule 3: a minor memorial site - Wikivoyage describes six new metal headstones inside a wire fence; nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it under See.

name: Lake Ballard
reason: Four counted sources (Wikivoyage Menzies and Kalgoorlie-Boulder; two Golden Outback board pages): Antony Gormley's 51 'Inside Australia' figures on the salt lake, an internationally known art site with walking and camping. Keep as one spot; any 'Inside Australia'/'Antony Gormley Sculptures' candidate is the same place.
objection: Remote (51 km of unsealed road from Menzies), but that is placement, not inclusion.

name: Niagara Dam
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Menzies See and Do with the 1.6 km Breakaway Trail and 1.1 km Round-the-Dam Trail; Golden Outback board 'a top rest stop on the Golden Quest Discovery Trail'): historic dam with walks, camping and picnics.
objection: An outback dam far down dirt roads; mostly a camping stop on a self-drive route.

name: Kookynie
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board lists the Kookynie Ruins (a 1903 town of 400+ buildings, now ruins), and Wikivoyage Menzies lists the Grand Hotel Kookynie; a ghost town to walk around with its historic pub, 2,336 page views.
objection: Only one counted source names the ruins as an attraction; little remains beyond the pub and scattered foundations.

name: Menzies Tank Hill
reason: Rule 2-3: Wikivoyage itself says 'there is not much to see up there' beyond an overview of the town; a short lookout with one source.
objection: It is a listed See item in a star Wikivoyage article.

name: Menzies Cemetery
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Menzies (star article) lists it with a distinctive feature - a dozen ornately cut tin headstones unique to the area.
objection: One counted source and a cemetery is a short look; friend test only if passing through Menzies.

name: Menzies Water Playground
reason: Rule 2-3: a children's splash playground, a local amenity like a suburban park, not a visitor draw.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under Do, and it is useful to families crossing the Goldfields in summer.

name: Hoover House
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger spot - Hoover House stands within the Gwalia historic site / Gwalia Museum precinct (the board describes it alongside the museum and the Oregon headframe), and it operates as a guest house; mention it in the Gwalia Museum spot.
objection: The board gives it its own listing and it has strong Herbert Hoover appeal; if Gwalia is not kept as a spot, this would need review.

name: The Terraces
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it twice (a large breakaway 40 km north-east of Leonora with bushwalking, camping and views in every direction).
objection: One counted source; remote unsealed access and no second guide naming it.

name: Malcolm Dam
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it (a 1902 railway dam near Leonora, a haven for birdwatchers).
objection: One counted source and a niche draw (birdwatching at a stock-type dam).

name: Leonora Loop Trails
reason: Not a place: two self-drive routes, each a day's driving; a route is how you see places, and its stops are the spots (COVERAGE 'A spot is a place').
objection: The board names them as a way to see the area.

name: Explorers Hall of Fame Laverton
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback board describes 'The Great Beyond - Explorers' Hall of Fame' as a state-of-the-art exhibition on the explorers and pioneers, housing the Laverton Visitor Centre; a museum visit of half an hour or more and the main sight in Laverton.
objection: Only one counted source; it doubles as the visitor centre and café. Name it 'The Great Beyond - Explorers' Hall of Fame' if kept.

name: Giles Breakaway
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it ('head out to the scenic Giles Breakaway for some great photo opportunities').
objection: One counted source, described only as a photo stop; no detail on walks or access.

name: Burtville
reason: Rule 1: Golden Outback board names it as a historic site of a former outback town near Laverton; a ghost town to explore, 587 page views.
objection: One counted source, mentioned in passing; little remains and access is by outback tracks.

name: Laverton Aboriginal Art Gallery
reason: Rule 2: primarily a shop (art and artefacts for sale) with one counted source; a venue that is only a shop fails.
objection: The board calls it a 'wonderful exhibition' with silk-dyeing demonstrations by arrangement; an Aboriginal art centre can be a cultural draw, so the owner may prefer review.

name: Golden Quest Discovery Trail
reason: Not a place: a 965 km self-drive touring route (Coolgardie-Menzies-Leonora-Laverton); its stops (Lake Ballard, Niagara Dam, Gwalia, Kookynie) are the spots. Mention it in descriptions.
objection: Two counted sources and heavy board branding; a long trail could be treated like a named drive.

name: Great Western Woodlands
reason: Rule 3 / not a place: a 16-million-hectare bioregion with no single visitor point; visitors experience it in the parks that are candidates in their own right (Goldfields Woodlands NP, Boorabbin NP, Burra Rock, Kalgoorlie Arboretum).
objection: 7,274 page views and Wikivoyage's Goldfields-Esperance page lists it under See/Do as the largest temperate woodland left on earth; it could suit a destination description.

name: Golden Pipeline Heritage Trail
reason: Not a place: a self-drive heritage route along the Mundaring-Kalgoorlie pipeline; its stops (pump stations, Mount Charlotte Reservoir) are the places.
objection: Has a National Trust and board presence and 845 page views.

name: CY O'Connor Pipeline
reason: Not a place: a 530 km water pipeline; it is seen at its stops, chiefly Mount Charlotte Reservoir and Lookout (Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder), so as a spot it is a duplicate of that.
objection: 10,605 page views and a famous engineering story; belongs in bios of Mount Charlotte / Mundaring Weir.

name: Eastern Goldfields Historical Society
reason: Rule 2-3: a research society and archive with limited opening, not a distinct visitor draw beside the Museum of the Goldfields; one counted source.
objection: The board lists it among Kalgoorlie attractions as holding a large range of historical material.

name: Natural Gold Nuggets and Jewellery

name: Norseman Beacon Hill Lookout

name: Norseman Historical Collection

name: Nullarbor Plain
reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Eyre Highway; Golden Outback board) and 88,149 page views: the Nullarbor crossing is a famous Australian draw; pin it at a visitor point, not a centroid.

name: Balladonia Cultural Heritage Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Golden Outback board names it (interactive displays on the area's history and the 1979 Skylab fall).

name: Twilight Cove

name: Old Homestead Cave

name: Boorabbin National Park

name: Goldfields Woodlands National Park

name: Goongarrie National Park

name: Peak Charles National Park

name: Frank Hann National Park

name: Matuwa Kurrara Kurrara National Park
reason: Rules 1 and 2 fail: no visitor page (the Parks WA URL is a 404) and the only reports (ExplorOz, 2024 forum) say traditional owners are not yet receiving visitors; camping and tourism not permitted.
objection: A new (2023) national park; if DBCA opens visitor access it should be reconsidered.

name: Credo Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page (bush walks, campground, salmon gum woodland, ghost-town relics, Rowles Lagoon, shearing shed); rule 2: open to the public.

name: Burra Rock Conservation Park

name: Gathercole Nature Reserve

reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page; rule 2: bushwalks, climb Boyagin Rock (50 m) for views, picnic, numbats and tammar wallabies. Kept as one spot with Boyagin Rock (same place, same point).

name: Mount Magnet Mining and Pastoral Museum

name: The Granites
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: a significant Aboriginal rock art site 7 km north of Mount Magnet; rule 2: open granite outcrop to explore.

name: Lennonville

name: Cue Heritage Discovery Centre

name: Big Bell Ghost Town
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Cue): ghost town of the early-1900s Big Bell mine; open-access ruins.

objection: None of note.

name: Charles Darwin Reserve
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Perenjori page names it (a Bush Heritage reserve of national ecological significance, 230 animal and 680 plant species, camping June-September at Samphire Campground, booked through Bush Heritage); Bush Heritage also runs guided visits.

name: Spider Orchard Wongan Hills
reason: Not a place: 'Spider Orchard' is a photo caption (a typo for spider orchid) on the Golden Outback Wongan Hills page; the wildflower places it names are Reynoldson's and Gathercole reserves and the Mount Matilda walk, which are the candidates to judge.
objection: Wongan Hills wildflowers are a real draw; check that Reynoldson's Flora Reserve is a candidate.

name: Kulin
reason: Town rule: Australia's Golden Outback gives Kulin its own page as 'the perfect base to explore the Eastern Wheatbelt', with the Tin Horse Highway, the Discovery Zone, the giant waterslide, Jilakin Rock and Buckley's Breakaway around it.
objection: Its main draw (the Tin Horse Highway) is a separate keep, so a Kulin town spot risks being a wrapper around it (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); the proposer may better use it as a base/destination name.

name: Corrigin
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Corrigin page gives it its own section as 'a popular stopover' on the way to Wave Rock: 'Town of Windmills', Pioneer Museum, Corrigin Rock and ANZAC lookouts, the Dog Cemetery, Gorge Rock and the Wildflower Drive.
objection: The best-known sight (Dog Cemetery) is a separate keep, so the town could be a wrapper; it is a stopover more than a base.

name: Southern Cross
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Southern Cross page gives it a section: a Golden Pipeline town on the Great Eastern Highway with the Yilgarn History Museum (open daily), Wimmera Hill Lookout, the pioneer cemetery and star-named streets, and accommodation; a stop between Perth and Kalgoorlie.
objection: Mainly a highway stop; its museum is a separate keep.

name: Sandstone
reason: Town rule: the Golden Outback Sandstone page gives it a section: gold-rush town with restored heritage buildings, the Sandstone Heritage Trail, the museum and visitor centre, London Bridge, the Peter Denny Lookout, and accommodation.
objection: Very remote and small; its headline sight, London Bridge, is a separate keep.

name: Tin Horse Highway
reason: Rule 1-3: a quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE names these as spots): Australia's Golden Outback has a product page (over 70 tin horses along about 15 km of road to the Jilakin race track, 'a quirky open-air gallery') and the Kulin page calls it the town's famous draw.
objection: A stretch of road rather than a point; pin it at the middle of the stretch. A drive-through of about 20 minutes, though people stop to photograph each horse.

name: West Kulin Tin Horses
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger spot: the tin horses on the western side of Kulin are 'an introduction to the Tin Horse Highway' (Golden Outback Kulin page), which is kept.
objection: None; mention them in the Tin Horse Highway bio.

name: Kulin Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it (Butler's Garage, one of Kulin's original buildings, with vintage cars, farm equipment and machinery).
objection: Open only on Saturday mornings and by appointment, so most visitors arrive to find it shut; one source; a small local museum.

name: Buckley's Breakaway
reason: Rule 1-3: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it as a picnic spot and 'a photographer's delight': orange clays against white cliffs and gullies, also a spring wildflower spot. A second-tier natural stop a real source names.
objection: One counted source only; no coordinates in the candidate, and the access is not described.

name: Kulin Giant Waterslide and Aquatic Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Kulin page names it as one of the three things Kulin is famous for ('regional Australia's biggest waterslide'); it is a seasonal venue (summer), which is allowed.
objection: It is the town's public swimming pool, a council facility mostly used by locals; one source.

name: Corrigin Dog Cemetery
reason: Rule 1-3: a quirky roadside icon with its own Australia's Golden Outback product page and a mention on the Corrigin page: a pet cemetery founded in 1974 with over 200 dogs, marked by a large dog statue, 5 km west of town on the Brookton Highway.
objection: A short stop (15-30 minutes); both counted mentions are from one board.

name: Corrigin Pioneer Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Corrigin page and its Dog Cemetery page name it (restored farm machinery, a pioneers' memorial wall).
objection: A small local museum with no hours found; one board only.

name: Corrigin Rock
reason: Rule 1: re-look found it named on the Golden Outback Corrigin page ('Take a walk up Corrigin Rock' for sunrise or sunset views of the town and farmland).
objection: A short lookout walk on a town outcrop, one passing mention; may be a 15-minute stop.

name: Dog in a Ute Statue
reason: no counted source after a re-look (web search found only Wikipedia, heritage/NRM records or community camping listings): fails rule 1 Only an aggregator (Visit Wanderland) mentions the chainsaw dog sculpture for the 2002 dogs-in-utes record; rule 3 also: a small statue, minor next to the Dog Cemetery.
objection: A fun photo stop tied to Corrigin's world record; could be mentioned in the Corrigin bio.

name: London Bridge
reason: Rule 1-3: two Golden Outback pages (its own product page: a 350-million-year-old natural rock arch 3 km south of Sandstone, a picnic and sunset spot for over 100 years, 'one of Sandstone's most iconic sights', dark-sky photography; and the Heritage Trail page). A distinct natural feature a guide singles out, not just a trail stop. DATA ERROR: the candidate's coordinates (51.508, -0.088) and 370,378 page views are London Bridge in England; re-resolve the pin near Sandstone (wiki 'London Bridge (Western Australia)' if it exists) and set views from the right article.
objection: A short visit (15-30 minutes) unless staying for sunset; it is one stop on the Sandstone Heritage Trail.

name: Sandstone Heritage Trail
reason: Not a place: an 18 km self-drive (plus town walk) linking Sandstone's buildings, London Bridge and the brewery site; its stops are judged separately (London Bridge kept) and the town (Sandstone, kept) covers the rest, so this is a duplicate of Sandstone.
objection: The board promotes it as a half-day outing, and the walking tours with a local guide are a real experience; the bio of Sandstone should mention it.

name: Sandstone Heritage Museum and Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: the Golden Outback Sandstone page names it (a small heritage museum attached to the visitor centre, gold-rush and pastoral memorabilia; it holds the key to the Black Range Chapel and its stained glass).
objection: Small, inside a visitor centre; one board; perhaps a 20-minute visit.

name: Tjukurba Art Gallery
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Golden Outback Wiluna page (historic photos and paintings by Martu artists who work in the gallery workshop) and the Shire of Wiluna tourism page ('a must', a working gallery where visitors meet the artists). Aboriginal art centre, a cultural draw.
objection: Partly a shop selling works; hours not found; small. Spelling varies (Tjukurba / Tjurkurba / Tjkurba).

name: Canning-Gunbarrel Discovery Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Golden Outback Wiluna page and the Shire of Wiluna tourism page (a museum in the restored old hospital on Wiluna's history, the Canning Stock Route and the Gunbarrel Highway; where travellers get the town map).
objection: Part visitor centre; modest in size.

name: Wiluna Red Hill Lookout
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Wiluna page names Red Hill Lookout, a rocky rise 1.2 km south of town with views over Wiluna to the gold mine.
objection: One source; a short lookout over a mine; probably under half an hour.

name: Wiluna Clay Pans
reason: Rule 4: only worth visiting after rain, when they fill (Golden Outback Wiluna page); not there whenever a visitor arrives, and only one passing mention.
objection: After rain they are a birding and picnic spot.

name: Wiluna North Pool
reason: Rule 1-2: two counted sources: the Shire of Wiluna tourism page (a peaceful waterhole 15 km out among red earth and gum trees, for a picnic, walk or sunset) and the Golden Outback Wiluna page (camping at North Pool). A second-tier natural stop.
objection: A local swimming/picnic waterhole; unofficial camping; access is on unsealed roads.

name: Last of the Nomads Statue
reason: Rule 1: the Golden Outback Wiluna page names it and tells its story at length (Warri and Yatungka, believed the last desert nomads, found in 1977); at the town entrance.
objection: A statue is a short photo stop and could fail rule 3 as a minor memorial; one source.

name: Wiluna Pioneer Cemetery
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage site given one line ('view the grave sites... 1893 to 1903') on the Golden Outback Wiluna page; not a draw a visitor goes out of their way for.
objection: None of note.

reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Wiluna, the town: a brochure walk around the town is how the town itself is seen, and belongs in the town's entry, not a separate spot (one source).
objection: Heritage walks are sometimes listed as spots; if Wiluna itself is not kept, this would be the way to represent it.

name: Yilgarn History Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Australia's Golden Outback has a product page: the museum in Southern Cross's 1892 courthouse (the first permanent courthouse in the Eastern Goldfields), with a working gold-battery model, a camel wagon and mining displays; the Southern Cross page says it is open daily.
objection: A small local museum; one board.

name: Pathways to Wave Rock
reason: Not a place: a 760 km self-drive trail through Wheatbelt towns to Wave Rock; Wave Rock and the towns are the spots.
objection: None.

name: Kalgoorlie-Boulder
reason: Rule 1-2: regional city with a full Wikivoyage guide (Super Pit, Hannan St heritage, museums, Mount Charlotte lookout) and a Golden Outback board page; the Goldfields' main base.
objection: Its headline sight (Super Pit) is a separate candidate; the city spot must stand for its streets and museums, not duplicate the pit.

name: Coolgardie
reason: Rule 1-2: historic gold-rush town with its own Wikivoyage guide (See listings incl. heritage buildings, Burra Rock further afield) and a board page; heritage main street to walk.
objection: Small town 40 km from Kalgoorlie; most visitors see it as a short stop on a Kalgoorlie trip.

name: Kambalda
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage guide and board page (Coolgardie & Kambalda) name the Red Hill Lookout over Lake Lefroy and land sailing; a stop with something to see.
objection: Thin: one lookout and a salt lake from a mining town; arguably marginal and could be a single 'Red Hill Lookout' spot instead of the town.

name: Norseman
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage guide and board page name the tin camels, historical collection, Beacon Hill views and the Dundas heritage drive; the gateway town to the Nullarbor.
objection: A junction/service town most pass through for fuel; the sights are modest.

name: Menzies
reason: Rule 1-2: substantial Wikivoyage guide (heritage buildings with information boards, visitor centre, Niagara Dam) and a board page; the base for Lake Ballard.

name: Leonora

name: Eucla

name: Hyden
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage guide and board page (Hyden & Wave Rock); the base for Wave Rock, Hippo's Yawn and The Humps.
objection: The town itself has little beyond its attractions 4-18 km away; it is close to being a wrapper for Wave Rock.

name: Merredin
reason: Rule 1-2: board page names Merredin Peak and the Golden Pipeline trail, the railway museum with signal tower, the Military Museum and the heritage Cummins Theatre; Wikivoyage Wheatbelt lists it.

name: Lucky Bay

name: Frenchman Peak

name: Hellfire Bay
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Cape Le Grand and the board (Esperance, Cape Le Grand) name it; a distinct beach and picnic spot, second-tier beaches keep.
objection: Third beach of the same park beside Lucky Bay; candidate has no coordinates yet.

name: Recherche Archipelago

name: Cape Le Grand National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA Explore Parks, the board and a full Wikivoyage park article; beaches, granite peaks and coast trail.
objection: None of substance; its headline beaches and peak are also candidates, so their photos and bios must not duplicate the park's.

name: Cape Arid National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA Explore Parks ('walk, swim, snorkel, fish, four-wheel drive or camp'), a Wikivoyage park article and the board Esperance page.

name: Super Pit Lookout
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder See listing (lookout off Mount Monger Rd, 7AM-7PM, information boards and old mining equipment) and the board page; one of the largest open-cut gold mines.
objection: The lookout is reached via Kalgoorlie and could be folded into the city; the mine itself is an industrial site.

name: Kanowna
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Kalgoorlie-Boulder listing: two cemeteries, a length of train platform, abandoned mines); the board Kalgoorlie page does not name it.
objection: Very little left to see on a flat plain; a 'only if nearby' stop. Case for: an authentic ghost town of a once 12,000-strong town, 29 km from Kalgoorlie.

name: Boulder Town Hall
reason: Rule 1-2: the board Kalgoorlie-Boulder page lists it (1908, beautifully preserved), and the hall holds the historic Goatcher stage curtain shown to visitors; one counted source.
objection: Rule 2: a civic building largely seen from the street; interior access and curtain viewings are limited, and Wikivoyage does not list it. Needs confirmation of public opening.

name: Menzies Town Hall
reason: Rule 2-3: a small heritage civic building on Menzies' main street (Wikivoyage: clock tower added late); seen from the street and part of the Menzies town spot, not a distinct half-hour draw.
objection: Wikivoyage calls it the most significant building in town and lists it as a See item.

name: Gwalia
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Leonora See listing (Gwalia Ghost Town, 9:30AM-4PM daily, Gwalia Museum) and the board Leonora & Gwalia page; museum in the old mine offices, Hoover House and preserved miners' cottages.
objection: 3 km from Leonora; arguably Leonora's own attraction, so the two must not duplicate.

name: Outback Way
reason: COVERAGE 'a spot is a place': a 2,700 km road from Laverton to Winton, mostly in the NT and Queensland; it is a way of travelling, and the places along it are the spots.
objection: The Laverton board page sells it as an epic 4WD odyssey (Australia's longest shortcut), the way a heritage drive can be the attraction itself.

name: Dundas
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Norseman Do listing (old town site, Dundas Rocks good to walk up for views, heritage route) and the board Norseman page (28 km Heritage Trail drive to Dundas Rocks); two counted sources. Its draw is Dundas Rocks, so the proposer should consider that name.
objection: Little remains of the town (a few placards); without the rocks it would be a pull-out.

name: Nullarbor Links
reason: COVERAGE 'a spot is a place' / Rule 3: an 18-hole golf course spread over 1,365 km of the Eyre Highway with holes at roadhouses in WA and SA; it is an activity with no single place to pin.
objection: Named by Wikivoyage Eyre Highway and the board as a quirky Nullarbor icon (15k views); individual holes could be mentioned in Norseman/Eucla bios.

name: Eyre Bird Observatory
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Eyre Highway side trip and the board Norseman-Nullarbor page; a BirdLife research station in the restored 1897 Eyre Telegraph Station that takes visitors.
objection: 4WD-only access south of Cocklebiddy and advance booking preferred; few visitors make the detour.

name: Bunda Cliffs
reason: Outside the region: the Bunda Cliffs and their signposted viewing spots run east of Eucla and Border Village, in South Australia (candidate coordinates 131.1 E); they belong to no WA region.
objection: Wikivoyage Eucla names them as a highlight of the drive; if the app covers South Australia they are a keep there.

name: Walga Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: obvious draw named by the board's Cue and Mount Magnet pages: a 1.5 km granite monolith with the largest gallery of Aboriginal rock paintings in WA and a cave to explore.
objection: Unsealed access 48 km west of Cue; one source family (the board), though two separate pages.

name: Wave Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: obvious draw; Wikivoyage Wave Rock and Hyden articles and the board page; a 15 m granite wave with walks around it.
objection: None of substance.

name: Hippo's Yawn
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Hyden and the board Hyden & Wave Rock page both name it; a gaping cavern in granite.
objection: Rule 3: it is 1 km from Wave Rock on the Wave Rock walk trail and is visited as part of the same stop (Wikivoyage suggests parking there and walking to Wave Rock); likely belongs in Wave Rock's bio rather than as its own spot.

name: The Humps
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Hyden (granite dome, trails with panels, Mulka's Cave with 450 handprints) and the board Hyden page (rock art at Mulka's Cave and The Humps). Kept as one place with Mulka's Cave.
objection: 18 km from Hyden on gravel; if Mulka's Cave is also a candidate it is a duplicate of this spot.

name: Totadgin Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1: named only by the regional board (Merredin and Hyden & Wave Rock pages: mini wave rock, interpretive trail, picnic spot); Wikivoyage Hyden does not mention it, so effectively one counted source.
objection: A small local conservation park 14 km from Merredin; 'mini wave rock' invites comparison with the real one an hour south; a stop only if nearby.

name: Dryandra Woodland
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA Explore Parks (Dryandra Woodland National Park) and the board Narrogin page: over 100 bird species, 24 mammal species including numbats, walks, wildflowers.
objection: None of substance.

name: Wiluna
reason: Rule 1-2: board Wiluna page and the Shire's tourism page name the Canning-Gunbarrel Discovery Centre (restored old hospital), Martu art gallery, heritage walk trails and Last of the Nomads statue; the gateway to the Canning Stock Route.
objection: Very remote; most visitors pass through as the start of a 4WD expedition.

name: Canning Stock Route
reason: Rule 1-2: the board Wiluna page and the Shire tourism page name it as one of Australia's iconic 4WD journeys (1,800 km); like a long-distance track, the route itself is the attraction. Boundary note: it starts at Wiluna (this region) but runs through the Pilbara and Kimberley; the proposer must dedupe with those regions and pin it per the track rule.
objection: A vehicle route rather than a place, multi-week, permits and expedition planning needed; arguably the wells and Durba Springs are the places.
